abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel paradigm shift for Internet of Things security by proposing a distributed trust management framework based on behavioral consensus mechanisms. Unlike conventional cryptographic approaches that rely on centralized certificate authorities, our theoretical framework establishes trust through peer-to-peer verification of device behavioral patterns. We formalize the trust propagation model using Markov chain theory and prove that the proposed consensus algorithm achieves convergence with probability approaching one under partial synchrony assumptions. The mathematical analysis demonstrates that our framework provides Byzantine fault tolerance while maintaining constant-time verification overhead, addressing the fundamental scalability limitations of existing blockchain-based IoT security solutions. Furthermore, we derive bounds on the minimum number of honest nodes required to maintain system integrity, which scales logarithmically with network size. Our theoretical contributions establish that behavioral consensus can achieve stronger security guarantees than traditional reputation systems while requiring fewer computational resources. The framework introduces formal verification conditions that enable autonomous security decisions without human intervention. This paradigm opens new research directions for designing IoT security protocols that are inherently distributed and resilient to sophisticated attacks.

This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical analysis of multi-user computation offloading in fog computing environments, significantly improving upon existing queuing theory models. We formulate the offloading decision problem as a Markov decision process with state-dependent energy costs and latency constraints. Our analysis introduces a novel reward function that balances computation efficiency against communication overhead, which existing studies have neglected. We derive closed-form expressions for the optimal offloading policy under various channel conditions, demonstrating that the proposed approach reduces average task completion time by 23-41% compared to greedy strategies. The theoretical analysis establishes that our method achieves near-optimal performance within 5% of the theoretically derived lower bound. We also provide rigorous proofs of policy convergence and analyze the computational complexity, showing linear scalability with the number of fog nodes. The derived theoretical results offer practical guidelines for parameter selection in real-world industrial IoT deployments. By incorporating mobility prediction into the decision framework, we extend the analysis to dynamic fog topologies. This work provides the theoretical foundation for implementing adaptive offloading systems in smart manufacturing applications.

This paper presents EdgeChain, a groundbreaking hierarchical edge-fog computing architecture that fundamentally redefines data processing in IoT ecosystems. The proposed system introduces a three-tier hierarchy consisting of device layer edge nodes, distributed fog clusters, and cloud coordination, enabling real-time analytics without cloud dependency. Unlike existing architectures that treat edge and fog as separate entities, EdgeChain establishes dynamic cooperative processing chains that adapt to workload characteristics in real-time. We implement a lightweight distributed ledger mechanism for maintaining processing provenance across heterogeneous nodes, ensuring data integrity while minimizing storage overhead by 67% compared to conventional blockchain approaches. The system incorporates intelligent task migration protocols that dynamically balance loads based on predicted computational requirements. Our prototype deployment across 150 nodes in a smart grid monitoring scenario demonstrates sub-10-millisecond response times for critical event detection. The architecture supports pluggable analytics modules through a standardized containerized interface, enabling flexible deployment of machine learning models at the edge. Security analysis confirms resilience against data tampering and unauthorized access. EdgeChain represents a paradigm shift toward autonomous, self-organizing IoT infrastructure that can operate effectively in disconnected or intermittently connected environments.

This paper presents EnergyOpt, an enhanced IoT platform specifically designed for smart city deployments that significantly improves energy efficiency through intelligent resource management. The system implements a novel adaptive sampling mechanism that dynamically adjusts sensor data collection rates based on environmental correlation analysis, reducing redundant transmissions by 78%. We design a hierarchical aggregation protocol that combines data from neighboring devices before fog processing, decreasing overall network traffic by 54%. EnergyOpt incorporates a machine learning-based prediction module that enables proactive resource scheduling, achieving 34% improvement in energy consumption per successfully delivered packet. The platform integrates seamlessly with existing LPWAN technologies and supports heterogeneous sensor types through a unified data model. We implement the complete system using off-the-shelf hardware components and deploy it across a pilot smart lighting network comprising 200 nodes. Real-world evaluation over six months demonstrates sustained operation with 41% extended node lifetime compared to conventional duty-cycling approaches. The system provides comprehensive monitoring dashboards for city administrators with real-time energy analytics. EnergyOpt addresses the critical challenge of maintaining large-scale IoT deployments by significantly reducing maintenance costs and environmental impact, making it particularly suitable for municipal infrastructure applications.
